overview: This file documents U.S. government consideration of phosphate deposits on Angaur Island from early postwar commercial inquiries in 1946 through an interdepartmental dispute in 1949 over continued mining for Japan. Initial correspondence concerns the Simpson Creek Collieries Company's unsuccessful effort to lease or purchase the mines while the former Japanese mandates remained under naval administration. Later Army, Navy, State, Defense, and Interior officials debated whether supplying phosphate for Japanese fertilizer needs justified damage to Angaur's agricultural land, groundwater, native resources, and future economy under the United Nations Trusteeship Agreement. The Army emphasized Japan's food crisis, existing investment, occupation costs, and local employment, while the Navy stressed Angaurese opposition, conservation, land rights, and the United States' obligations to the Trust Territory.

subfiles.title: Alien Property Custodian referral of Simpson Creek inquiry
subfiles.from: Raoul Berger, General Counsel, Office of Alien Property Custodian
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, attention Legal Adviser
subfiles.about: Berger forwards a private company's inquiry about Angaur phosphate deposits and a copy of his response for State Department action.
subfiles.summary: Alien Property Custodian forwards Simpson Creek Collieries' inquiry and a reply, judging the matter falls under State's jurisdiction to answer.

subfiles.title: Alien Property Custodian reply to Simpson Creek Collieries
subfiles.from: Raoul Berger, General Counsel, Office of Alien Property Custodian
subfiles.to: The Simpson Creek Collieries Co., Inc.
subfiles.about: Berger informs the company that its proposal to exploit Angaur phosphate has been referred to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Berger tells Simpson Creek Collieries its interest in Angaur phosphate deposits has been referred to State, which has jurisdiction to reply directly.

subfiles.title: Simpson Creek inquiry about Angaur phosphate deposits
subfiles.from: The Simpson Creek Collieries Co., Inc.
subfiles.about: The company asks how it may obtain access to Angaur phosphate deposits for superphosphate production.
subfiles.summary: Simpson Creek, planning to make superphosphate, asks whether Angaur's deposits (believed enemy property) are available, seeking assistance or the right agency.

subfiles.title: State Department response on private operations in former mandates
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Department of State
subfiles.to: The Simpson Creek Collieries Co., Inc.
subfiles.about: Martin explains that private companies cannot yet operate in Angaur or the other former Japanese mandates.
subfiles.summary: Martin explains Angaur is a former Japanese mandate under Naval Military Government, where no private business is yet permitted pending fair, open-trade facilities; trade will open under normal U.S. policy when conditions allow.

subfiles.title: State Department referral of leasing request to the Navy
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Department of State
subfiles.to: The Simpson Creek Collieries Co., Inc.
subfiles.about: State refers the company's request to negotiate a lease or purchase of the Angaur mines to the Navy Department.
subfiles.summary: Martin tells Simpson Creek its request to negotiate immediately for the Angaur mines, despite the ban on private operations, has been forwarded to the Navy, which administers the island.

subfiles.title: Simpson Creek request to negotiate for the Angaur mines
subfiles.from: The Simpson Creek Collieries Co., Inc., signed by R. Seyler
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin, Department of State
subfiles.about: The company asks to negotiate a conditional lease or purchase before private trade with Angaur is reopened.
subfiles.summary: Simpson Creek, acknowledging private trade is temporarily barred, seeks to begin negotiating a lease or purchase of the Angaur phosphate mines pending the Navy's eventual disposal decision.

subfiles.title: Army transmittal of its position on Angaur mining
subfiles.from: John P. Loomis, Office of the Administrator for Occupied Areas
subfiles.about: Loomis sends State a copy of the Army's letter to the Secretary of the Navy advocating continued phosphate mining.
subfiles.summary: Army forwards State its August 11 reply on Angaur phosphate mining, following a July 1 Navy letter to the Army, for United Nations-related disposition.

subfiles.title: Signed copy of Army transmittal to State
subfiles.from: John P. Loomis, Food Administrator for Occupied Areas
subfiles.about: This clean signed copy repeats the Army's transmittal of its response to the Navy on Angaur mining.
subfiles.summary: Copy records Loomis forwarding the Army's reply to the Navy Secretary, answering the Acting Navy Secretary's July 1 letter to the Army.

subfiles.title: Army case for continuing phosphate mining on Angaur
subfiles.from: John P. Loomis, Food Administrator for Occupied Areas
subfiles.about: The Army asks the Navy to reconsider its opposition and permit Angaur phosphate mining to continue for the life of the existing agreement.
subfiles.summary: Army, citing SCAP cables, disputes claims mining threatens Angaur's farmland and groundwater, citing unused taro land, a $268,000 Japanese investment, an $8 million replacement cost if mining stops, native employment benefits, and compatibility with the Trusteeship Agreement.

subfiles.title: Conversation on possible discontinuance of Angaur mining
subfiles.to: Department of State file and listed offices
subfiles.about: State, Defense, and Navy officials discuss resolving the Army-Navy disagreement over Angaur phosphate mining.
subfiles.summary: Cargo and Yeomans brief Young that any Angaur decision must withstand Trusteeship Council scrutiny; Germershausen presents Navy and Geological Survey evidence, and Young agrees Defense should take next steps toward settlement, with a visiting mission likely to examine the dispute.

subfiles.title: Navy argument for terminating Angaur phosphate mining
subfiles.from: Francis P. Matthews, Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.to: Gordon Gray, Secretary of the Army
subfiles.about: Matthews presents the Navy's detailed case that U.S. trusteeship obligations require early termination of phosphate mining on Angaur.
subfiles.summary: Matthews reports that a conference among Army, Navy, and Interior representatives failed because the Army prioritized inexpensive fertilizer for Japan while the Navy and Interior prioritized obligations to the Trust Territory's inhabitants. He reviews the postwar reopening of the mines, naval objections, the importation of Japanese labor, the Hopkins Committee's conservation recommendation, and a Geological Survey warning that mining destroys scarce agricultural land and may damage groundwater. He emphasizes unresolved land title, repeated Angaurese objections, the High Commissioner's criticism, and a Trusteeship Council resolution questioning the export arrangement and its 25-cent royalty. Predicting exhaustion of the deposits within about five years just as regional fertilizer demand rises, Matthews asks the Army to agree to early termination.

interest: Shows postwar conflict between rebuilding Japan's phosphate-mining economy and protecting Pacific trust-territory islanders' resources.
